newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-MANCHESTER CITY LINE UP TIE WITH MIDDLESBROUGH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MANCHESTER CITY LINE UP TIE WITH MIDDLESBROUGH.

text.p: Two second half goals inside 10 minutes by Nicky Summerbee and Uwe Roesler lifted beleaguered Manchester City to a 3-1 win over second division Watford in an English F.A. Cup fourth round match on Wednesday.

But it was not until Summerbee's 61st-minute strike put the lowly first division side 2-1 ahead that City took control, despite Watford being reduced to 10 men when defender Steve Palmer was sent off shortly after the interval.
Roesler's goal 10 minutes later set up the northern club for a lucrative home tie against premier league strugglers Middlesbrough in the next round.
Neil Heaney had put City ahead in the first half, deflecting a shot from Kit Symons over the line from point-blank range, for his first goal for City since signing from Southampton in November.
The visitors suffered a major blow after 53 minutes when Palmer aimed a needless punch at Steve Lomas and was immediately ordered off by the referee.
But despite this setback, Watford drew level after 58 minutes when 17-year-old striker Gifton Noel-Williams danced round City goalkeeper Martyn Margetson before hammering the ball home.

But Watford's hopes were short lived. City regained the lead three minutes later, Summerbee feeding Georgi Kinkladze and then taking the Georgian's return pass to drive sweetly past keeper Kevin Miller from 10 metres.
